entries.title: keep Http1Connection's per-request path on hot fields
entries.body:
Http1Connection's fields are reordered so that the per-request methods (inputRoom, feed, next, respond, write, end, consume, release, park) read the first two cache lines of the object instead of three. A new outputCap field mirrors output.length, so acquire and release no longer read the resting connection's empty output array, which is cold. inputRoom reads ws and config only in the WebSocket state. The object stays 184 bytes with no padding warning, and no limit, rule, status or wire byte changes.

bench/http1-conn times the connection with no socket, comparing old, a byte-identical copy of old as the noise band, and new.

Measured: hot 0.971x ns/request (noise band 1.012x, 21 rounds); cold 0.988x within noise (0.990x); cachegrind cold D1 misses 35.0 -> 33.4 per request
Tests: tests/link/net_http1_server/conn.ts
Part of #1175
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: pin and baseline the Http1Connection benchmark
entries.body:
bench/http1-conn/run.mjs now runs each timed binary under `taskset -c 1`
when taskset works, and says "unpinned (no taskset)" when it does not;
before, it only probed for taskset and reported a pin it never applied.
The `--base` default is the commit before the hot-field layout (96a38347),
so the benchmark compares old against new on main instead of new against
itself. The header comment's `--requests` default matches the code.
metrics: pinned, 15 rounds, ns/request median: hot old 591.6, old′ 594.9 (1.005), new 568.5 (0.961); cold old 677.5, old′ 663.6 (0.979), new 650.5 (0.960)

entries.title: measure SHA-256's block function against OpenSSL and hold HMAC to it under both NISH_SHA256 settings
entries.body:
The scalar body (NISH_SHA256=soft) is 13.9% to 22.1% slower than OpenSSL 3.0's scalar
sha256_block_data_order on a Xeon @ 2.1 GHz, and ~40% slower than its AVX2 body.
The best source rewrite gained 8-9.4%, under the 10% bar, so sha256Compress is
unchanged. The obstacle is the compiler: module-level constant arrays are refused,
so the K table cannot drive a rolled round loop. HMAC-SHA256, HS256 and
hmacCopySha256 (PBKDF2) all reach the SHA-NI kernel by default and the Nish body
under NISH_SHA256=soft, and a Node-crypto differential now pins both.
bench/sha256-block/ reruns the table and the variants on a CPU without SHA-NI.
metrics: soft 208-218 ns/block, OpenSSL scalar 174-183, AVX2 148-151, SHA-NI 47-49 (Nish) / 42 (OpenSSL); copy band 0.7-2.3%

entries.title: scan HTTP/1.1 request heads a vector at a time
entries.body:
The request parser in nish/net/http1-codec no longer walks a line a byte at
a time.

- The line scan jumps straight to the first control byte or DEL of each
  16-byte block: the lowest set bit of a SWAR mask, exact because a borrow
  only carries upward from a true match.
- A CRLF is taken in one step.
- The token check is a branch-free lookup in a 128-bit tchar table instead
  of a chain of comparisons. The client codec shares it.
- A field name is lowercased while it is scanned in the head copy.

No limit, status or reason string changed.

tests/link/net_http1_parse_diff proves the parity. It runs main's parser,
frozen by bench/http1-parse/freeze.mjs, beside the live one on 190,276
cases and fails on the first difference in any event, status, reason,
field, span or body window:
- the fuzz corpus;
- every byte value at every position;
- every limit at max−1, max and max+1;
- every split and byte-at-a-time feed;
- pipelined pairs;
- 100,000 seeded grammar cases.
A deliberately broken http1FirstByte fails it.

bench/http1-parse times the parser old against old′ (a byte-identical copy
that gives the noise band) against new, interleaved.
metrics: Xeon @ 2.1 GHz container, ns/head median. loadgen GET (337 B) −15.2% vs old, −17.9% vs old′ (band 3.3%); POST (447 B) −26.1% / −18.2% (band 9.6%); browser GET (1,028 B, 16 fields) −21.2% / −25.4% (band 5.7%). Instructions/head −15% to −16% (per byte 16.7→14.2, 17.4→14.5, 15.9→13.3).

entries.title: add nish:simd lane operations, masks and constant-count shifts and rotates
entries.body:
* feat(checker): add nish:simd lane operations, masks and constant shifts (wip)

Work in progress on the WP38 S3 ops stage: lane arithmetic, compares
answering masks, select, any/all/bitmask, sum, shuffle, and shl/shr/
rotl/rotr by a constant count below the lane width. Goldens, codes and
docs follow.

* wip(simd): ops-stage docs, codes, goldens and the ARX bench

Work in progress on the nish:simd operations stage; the goldens,
lint and benchmark figures follow before the pull request.

* test(self): register the nish:simd ops cases with the differential goldens

* refactor(codegen): name the shift opcode without a nested ternary

* test(self): regenerate the checked goldens for the nish:simd ops stage

* test(self): regenerate the simd and types goldens after the lint fix

* fix(interop): give addWrapping and subWrapping their own bodies in runtime/core.mjs

knip refuses an export that aliases another as a duplicate.

Tests: tests/cases/simd_ops_int

* fix(self): keep nish:simd's checker and intrinsic table under the performance ratchet

The vector intrinsic table called vectorSuffix inside its loops, which left
its scratch strings behind on every pass (NL9011, five sites in
src/runtime.ts); the suffixes are now written beside their types. The
shuffle-index check widened an i32 product after computing it (NL9005) and
indexed args again inside the loop (NL9007). Declarations are unchanged.

Tests: tests/run.js self (performance ratchet), simd, performance

entries.title: ChaCha20 keystream on AVX2 and NEON behind a CPU check
entries.body:
* test(bench): measure ChaCha20 on vectors against the Nish AEAD

WP38 S10's measure. bench/chacha20.ts times ChaCha20-Poly1305 seal and open
at 64 B, 1 KiB, 16 KiB and 1 MiB, and each half alone on 16 KiB, against a
copy of the std file whose keystream loop hands four blocks or more to
bench/chacha20/kernel.c: a C scalar copy, four blocks in portable
vector_size(16) C, eight in AVX2 behind a CPUID check, and four in NEON.
bench/chacha20.mjs holds every path to the scalar reference and RFC 8439's
vector, times them in interleaved rounds with a copy column for the noise
band, and judges both routes' bars. CI's simd-arm64 job prints the NEON
figures.

Refs: docs/wp38-simd.md#31-runtime-kernels

* perf(runtime): ChaCha20 keystream kernel, work in progress

* perf(runtime): ChaCha20 keystream on AVX2 and NEON behind a CPU check

ChaCha20-Poly1305's keystream now runs in runtime/runtime-chacha20.c
when the message is 256 bytes or more and the CPU has the vectors:
eight blocks at a time in AVX2 on x86-64, then four in 128-bit lanes,
or four with NEON on little-endian AArch64. The compiler recognises
std/crypto/chacha20poly1305.ts's chacha20XorInto seam (src/kernels.ts)
and calls nish_chacha20_xor. The Nish code stays as the fallback for
short messages, other CPUs, wasm32 and NISH_CHACHA20=soft.

WP38 S10 measured both routes first. The runtime kernel cleared its bar
(at least 20% in two runs beyond the noise band) at every size from
1 KiB. The portable 128-bit route peaked at 1.26x on the AEAD, short
of nish:simd's 1.5x bar, so no nish:simd version is planned. Poly1305
in C was within the noise band and stays in Nish.

The kernel uses no secret-dependent branch or index. It wipes its
keystream and state copies before it returns. The record is
docs/security/crypto-chacha20-hw.md.

Measured: seal 1 MiB 278 -> 635 MB/s (2.30x), band 3.9%; AVX2 gained 39-60% at >=1 KiB in two runs, band 0.7-5.5%
Refs: docs/wp38-simd.md#s10-chacha20-on-vectors
Tests: tests/simd/chacha20.c, tests/link/chacha20_hw_agree

* docs(self): say which S10 figures are medians

* docs(codegen): regenerate the IR cookbook for the ChaCha20 kernel declarations
